order.title: The living worlds, healthiest first
order.caption: Each of the 82 worlds that lived to the end of its run is a row, in the order of its health by the product of its six criteria; each criterion is a column, coloured by the world's score in it, from dark (worse than nearly every world) to bright yellow (better than every other). A world named "w" or "s" is one of the eight draws played a token at a time, weakest first or strongest first. The 18 worlds that died are not shown: they come last in every order.
order.recipe:
**Runs.** every world of round 3 of the screen of random worlds (Experiments 40, 41 and 42: 100 worlds of 30,000 tokens, played for 3,000 iterations)

**Data.** From the screen's readings of every world, `GraphOfLifeRuns/.pilots/screen/worlds/<run>.json` (research/screen/measures.py: every iteration's statistics, every 25th iteration's frame, every kept world), and each run's own statistics for its culls, scored by `research/screen/health.py` into `research/screen/health.json`.

1. Average every measure of a world over iterations 100 to the end of its run (the judge's averages, `research/screen/measures.py`).
2. Score each measure by the share of the living worlds the world does better than (`shares` in `health.py`): the best 1, the worst 1/82, ties sharing their place.
3. Each criterion: the geometric mean of its measures' scores. Health: the six criteria multiplied (as their geometric average), added (as their average), or the worst of them.
4. Rank the living worlds by the product, ties by their weakest criterion.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py healthorder`.

measures.title: Every measure, against the living worlds
measures.caption: One chart a measure: each dot is a living world's average of it, from iteration 100 to the end of its run; the short bar is the median. The title says which criterion the measure belongs to and which way is better. A world's score in a measure is the share of the other worlds it does better than, so only the order of the dots counts. The dots are spread sideways only so that they do not hide each other.
measures.recipe:
**Runs.** every world of round 3 of the screen of random worlds (Experiments 40, 41 and 42: 100 worlds of 30,000 tokens, played for 3,000 iterations)

**Data.** From the screen's readings of every world, `GraphOfLifeRuns/.pilots/screen/worlds/<run>.json` (research/screen/measures.py: every iteration's statistics, every 25th iteration's frame, every kept world), and each run's own statistics for its culls, scored by `research/screen/health.py` into `research/screen/health.json`.

1. Read each living world's averages from `health.json`.
2. One dot per world and measure.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py healthorder`.

culls.title: Leaves or branches: what the worlds lose in their culls
culls.caption: Each dot is a living world, averaged over the games from iteration 100 to the end of its run. Across, the share of its agents a game culls (cuts off from the largest piece of the network and removes); up, the share of all the world's tokens those agents held. On the dashed diagonal the culled hold as much as the average agent does. Below it they hold less: leaves, poor agents cut off at the edge. On it and above, they are whole branches, with all they held. Agents that starved are not counted: they hold nothing.
culls.recipe:
**Runs.** every world of round 3 of the screen of random worlds (Experiments 40, 41 and 42: 100 worlds of 30,000 tokens, played for 3,000 iterations)

**Data.** From each run's own statistics, `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/stats.jsonl` (the game phase's cleanup: `orphaned`, `redistributed`, `nodes`, `starved`), read by `research/screen/health.py` into `research/screen/health.json`.

1. For every game: the agents culled over the agents just before the cleanup (those left, the starved and the culled), and the tokens shared out by the cleanup over all the world's tokens (the starved hold none, so every token shared out was a culled agent's).
2. Average both over the games from iteration 100 to the end of the run.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py healthorder`.

halves.title: Healthier or sicker with time?
halves.caption: Each dot is a living world: its health by the product, scored over the first half of its run (iterations 100 to the middle) and over the second (the middle to the end), every half against every half of every world. Above the dashed diagonal a world grew healthier; below it, sicker.
halves.recipe:
**Runs.** every world of round 3 of the screen of random worlds (Experiments 40, 41 and 42: 100 worlds of 30,000 tokens, played for 3,000 iterations)

**Data.** From the screen's readings of every world, `GraphOfLifeRuns/.pilots/screen/worlds/<run>.json` (research/screen/measures.py: every iteration's statistics, every 25th iteration's frame, every kept world), and each run's own statistics for its culls, scored by `research/screen/health.py` into `research/screen/health.json`.

1. Average every measure of each half of every living world's run.
2. Score all the halves together, as the whole runs are scored.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py healthorder`.
